cards.hypothesis: Subjects with high inter-beat interval (IBI) variability during baseline exhibit undercoverage because their stress-induced IBI shifts fall outside the Mondrian taxonomy's calibration quantiles.
cards.proposed_mechanism: High baseline IBI variability widens the conformal prediction intervals during calibration, but the Mondrian taxonomy bins subjects by mean IBI rather than variability, causing miscalibrated intervals for high-variability subjects when stress induces non-linear IBI shifts.
cards.causal_path: High baseline IBI variability (RMSSD > 50ms) → widened calibration intervals in Mondrian bin → stress-induced non-linear IBI shift exceeds interval bounds → undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is driven by sensor noise during stress, not baseline variability.
cards.rival_prediction: Signal quality index (SQI) during stress predicts undercoverage better than baseline RMSSD.
cards.distinguishing_test: Regress coverage_indicator on baseline_RMSSD and stress_SQI simultaneously; H1 predicts baseline_RMSSD remains significant (p<0.05) while stress_SQI does not.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior WESAD analyses show RMSSD-stress reactivity correlations of r≈0.4-0.5; Mondrian binning adds discretization error.
minimum_data_needed: WESAD ECG chest signals for baseline and stress conditions
Mondrian taxonomy bin assignments per subject
Conformal prediction intervals and coverage outcomes per trial
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with baseline RMSSD > 50ms will show coverage rates at least 15 percentage points below nominal (e.g., <75% for 90% nominal).
cards.failure_condition: No significant difference in coverage between high-RMSSD (>50ms) and low-RMSSD (<30ms) groups (two-proportion z-test, p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Two-proportion z-test comparing coverage rates between high/low baseline RMSSD groups; logistic regression with coverage as outcome and baseline RMSSD as predictor controlling for age/fitness.
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian with variability-aware taxonomy (bin by RMSSD quintiles); if undercoverage persists for high-RMSSD subjects, the mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Wrist-worn EDA sensor detachment during stress-induced movement causes signal dropout that the Mondrian taxonomy fails to detect, leading to undercoverage for high-movement subjects.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Stress conditions (TSST) increase upper-body movement → wrist EDA sensor loses skin contact → EDA signal drops to near-zero → Mondrian taxonomy (based on EDA mean/phasic power) assigns these trials to wrong bins → prediction intervals computed from clean calibration data don't cover dropout-corrupted test points.
cards.causal_path: Stress-induced movement → wrist EDA sensor detachment → EDA signal dropout (amplitude < 0.01 μS) → incorrect Mondrian bin assignment → prediction interval mismatch → undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage stems from chest EDA sensor artifacts, not wrist detachment.
cards.rival_prediction: Chest EDA SQI predicts undercoverage; wrist ACC does not.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare logistic regression models: Model A (wrist_ACC + wrist_EDA_SQI) vs Model B (chest_EDA_SQI); H2 predicts Model A has significantly better AIC.
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD documentation notes wrist EDA dropout during movement; Mondrian has no dropout detection mechanism.
minimum_data_needed: WESAD wrist ACC and EDA signals
cards.testable_prediction: Trials with wrist ACC magnitude > 1.5g and wrist EDA amplitude < 0.01 μS will have coverage rates < 60% at 90% nominal.
cards.failure_condition: Coverage rates for high-movement/dropout trials do not differ from low-movement trials (p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Mixed-effects logistic regression: coverage ~ wrist_ACC * wrist_EDA_amplitude + (1|subject); test interaction term significance.
cards.falsification_test: Impute dropout trials using chest EDA; if undercoverage persists for high-movement subjects, wrist detachment mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Non-stationary EDA phasic driver rates during prolonged stress exposure violate Mondrian's exchangeability assumption within taxonomy bins.
cards.proposed_mechanism: During the 10-minute TSST stressor, EDA phasic driver rate (SCR frequency) increases then habituates non-linearly → Mondrian taxonomy bins by mean phasic power over entire calibration window → test trials from late stress phase have different distribution than calibration trials → conformal intervals miscalibrated.
cards.causal_path: Prolonged stress exposure → time-varying EDA phasic driver rate (non-stationary) → Mondrian bin assumes stationarity → calibration distribution ≠ test distribution → undercoverage for late-phase trials
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to inter-subject differences in mean phasic level, not intra-subject non-stationarity.
cards.rival_prediction: Subject-level mean phasic power predicts undercoverage; within-subject time trend does not.
cards.distinguishing_test: Fit mixed model: coverage ~ stress_phase_minute + subject_mean_phasic + (1|subject); H3 predicts stress_phase_minute significant (p<0.01), subject_mean_phasic not.
cards.effect_size_rationale: EDA habituation literature shows 30-50% SCR rate decline over 10min; Mondrian bins ignore temporal structure.
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage rate declines by ≥20 percentage points from minute 1 to minute 10 of TSST within the same Mondrian bin.
cards.failure_condition: No significant negative slope of coverage vs. stress_phase_minute (linear mixed model, p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage_indicator ~ stress_phase_minute + (1|subject) + (1|mondrian_bin); test fixed effect of minute.
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian using only early-stress (min 1-3) calibration data; if late-stress coverage improves to nominal, non-stationarity mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Self-report stress labels (VAS) contain systematic bias for high-alexithymia subjects, causing Mondrian to learn incorrect stress-response mappings.
cards.proposed_mechanism: High alexithymia subjects under-report stress on VAS despite physiological arousal → Mondrian taxonomy uses VAS as ground truth for calibration → prediction intervals trained on mismatched (physiology, label) pairs → undercoverage when true physiological stress exceeds reported level.
cards.causal_path: High alexithymia (TAS-20 > 60) → VAS stress rating underestimation → Mondrian learns attenuated physiology-label mapping → prediction intervals too narrow for true stress level → undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage reflects true physiological non-response (low reactivity), not label noise.
cards.rival_prediction: Physiological stress index (ECG+EDA composite) will be low for undercovered high-alexithymia subjects.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare physiological_stress_index between high-alexithymia undercovered vs. covered subjects; H4 predicts undercovered group has HIGHER physiological stress (t-test p<0.05).
cards.effect_size_rationale: No prior WESAD analysis links alexithymia to conformal coverage; need TAS-20 scores which WESAD lacks. Would require new data collection with TAS-20.
cards.testable_prediction: High-alexithymia subjects (TAS-20>60) with VAS<50 but physiological_stress_index>75th percentile will show coverage <70% at 90% nominal.
cards.failure_condition: No coverage difference between high/low alexithymia groups after controlling for physiological_stress_index (ANCOVA p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: ANCOVA: coverage_rate ~ alexithymia_group + physiological_stress_index; test group effect.
cards.falsification_test: Re-train Mondrian using physiological_stress_index as label instead of VAS; if undercoverage disappears for high-alexithymia subjects, label-noise mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian taxonomy based on marginal feature quantiles fails to capture subject-specific multivariate physiological response patterns, causing undercoverage for subjects with atypical response profiles.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Mondrian bins use univariate quantiles of EDA mean, ECG mean, etc. → subjects with atypical multivariate patterns (e.g., high EDA + low HRV) fall in bins dominated by typical responders → calibration intervals reflect typical pattern, not atypical subject's conditional distribution → undercoverage.
cards.causal_path: Atypical multivariate response profile → assignment to typical-responder Mondrian bin → calibration intervals mismatch subject's true conditional distribution → undercoverage
control_variables: ensure minimum 30 calibration trials per bin
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to insufficient calibration data per subject, not taxonomy structure.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage improves monotonically with calibration set size regardless of response typicality.
cards.distinguishing_test: For subjects with fixed calibration size (n=30), compare coverage between typical (Mahalanobis distance <1) vs atypical (>2) responders; H5 predicts atypical worse (p<0.01).
cards.effect_size_rationale: Multivariate atypicality in WESAD: ~15% subjects show discordant EDA/HRV responses; Mondrian univariate bins cannot capture this.
minimum_data_needed: WESAD multi-signal features (EDA, ECG, RESP, TEMP)
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with Mahalanobis distance >2 from bin centroid in feature space will have coverage ≤70% at 90% nominal, while typical responders (distance<1) achieve ≥85%.
cards.failure_condition: No coverage difference between typical and atypical responders within same bin and calibration size (p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Quantile regression: coverage_rate ~ mahalanobis_distance + calibration_size + bin_id; test distance coefficient.
cards.falsification_test: Replace Mondrian with multivariate k-NN taxonomy; if undercoverage for atypical subjects resolves, univariate taxonomy mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Temporal autocorrelation in physiological residuals violates the exchangeability assumption of conformal prediction, causing undercoverage for subjects with high residual autocorrelation.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Physiological signals exhibit AR(1) residual structure after Mondrian point prediction → conformal prediction assumes i.i.d. residuals → prediction intervals too narrow for high-autocorrelation subjects → undercoverage proportional to autocorrelation magnitude.
cards.causal_path: High residual AR(1) coefficient (φ > 0.5) → effective sample size reduction → conformal quantile underestimates true variability → prediction intervals too narrow → undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to heteroscedasticity, not autocorrelation.
cards.rival_prediction: Residual variance (not AR1) predicts undercoverage; AR1 coefficient adds no predictive value.
cards.distinguishing_test: Regress coverage_indicator on residual_AR1 and residual_variance; H6 predicts AR1 significant (p<0.01), variance not significant when both included.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Conformal prediction is robust to mild autocorrelation; effect only large for φ>0.7 which is rare in preprocessed physiology.
minimum_data_needed: Mondrian point predictions and residuals per trial
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with residual AR1 > 0.6 will show coverage ≤80% at 90% nominal; subjects with AR1 < 0.2 will achieve ≥88%.
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between subject-level AR1 coefficient and coverage rate (Spearman ρ, p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Spearman correlation between subject-level residual AR1 and coverage rate; permutation test (n=10000) for significance.
cards.falsification_test: Apply block conformal prediction (block length = 1/AR1); if coverage reaches nominal for high-AR1 subjects, autocorrelation mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Subjects with delayed physiological recovery post-stress show undercoverage because Mondrian calibration includes recovery-phase data that contaminates stress-phase intervals.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Slow recoverers (EDA/HRV return to baseline >15min) have prolonged stress physiology → Mondrian calibration pools stress and recovery trials → stress-phase test trials compared to contaminated calibration distribution → intervals too wide for stress, too narrow for recovery → undercoverage specifically for stress-phase trials of slow recoverers.
cards.causal_path: Slow physiological recovery (recovery_time_constant > 15min) → calibration set mixes stress/recovery → stress-phase test distribution ≠ calibration distribution → miscalibrated intervals → stress-phase undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage affects all phases equally for slow recoverers, not just stress phase.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage equally low for stress and recovery phases in slow recoverers.
cards.distinguishing_test: Two-way ANOVA: coverage ~ recovery_group (slow/fast) * test_phase (stress/recovery); H7 predicts significant interaction (p<0.01).
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD recovery data shows ~30% subjects have τ>15min; calibration contamination effect estimated 10-15% coverage drop.
minimum_data_needed: WESAD physiological signals during stress AND 30min recovery
cards.testable_prediction: Slow recoverers (τ>15min) show stress-phase coverage ≤75% but recovery-phase coverage ≥85% at 90% nominal; fast recoverers show ≥85% for both.
cards.failure_condition: No interaction between recovery_group and test_phase on coverage (p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Mixed-effects logistic regression: coverage ~ recovery_group * test_phase + (1|subject); test interaction.
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian using ONLY stress-phase data; if slow-recoverer stress-phase coverage reaches nominal, contamination mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Chest-worn sensor displacement during TSST social-evaluative threat causes ECG/RESP artifact bursts that Mondrian taxonomy misclassifies as extreme stress responses.
cards.proposed_mechanism: TSST induces posture shifts/gestures → chest sensor belt loosens → ECG/RESP artifacts (flatlines, saturation) → Mondrian taxonomy (using ECG/RESP features) assigns artifact trials to 'extreme stress' bins → prediction intervals from true extreme stress don't cover artifact-corrupted test points → undercoverage.
cards.causal_path: TSST social-evaluative threat → posture shifts → chest belt displacement → ECG/RESP artifacts → incorrect Mondrian bin assignment (extreme stress bin) → prediction interval mismatch → undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is from wrist sensor artifacts, not chest.
cards.rival_prediction: Wrist ACC/artifact flags predict undercoverage; chest ACC/artifacts do not.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare AUC of logistic models: chest_artifact_model vs wrist_artifact_model for predicting undercoverage; H8 predicts chest model AUC > wrist model AUC by ≥0.15.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Chest belt displacement is documented in WESAD; ECG artifacts directly corrupt HRV features used in Mondrian bins.
minimum_data_needed: WESAD chest ACC, ECG, RESP signals
cards.testable_prediction: Trials with chest ECG artifact flag=1 and chest ACC>1g will have coverage <50% at 90% nominal.
cards.failure_condition: Artifact-flagged trials show coverage not significantly different from clean trials (p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Fisher's exact test: coverage (yes/no) vs artifact_flag (yes/no) stratified by chest_ACC tertile.
cards.falsification_test: Remove artifact-flagged trials from calibration and test; if undercoverage disappears for high-chest-ACC subjects, mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian's fixed taxonomy bins create insufficient calibration samples for rare physiological phenotypes, causing undercoverage for subjects in sparsely populated bins.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Mondrian taxonomy creates 20 bins from marginal quantiles → some bins contain <10 calibration trials for rare phenotypes (e.g., high EDA + low HRV + high TEMP) → conformal quantile estimation unstable → intervals too narrow (undercoverage) or erratic.
cards.causal_path: Rare multivariate phenotype → sparse Mondrian bin (n_calibration < 15) → high variance in conformal quantile estimate → prediction intervals systematically too narrow → undercoverage
control_variables: fix total calibration size per subject
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to phenotype extremity (outlier-ness), not bin sparsity.
cards.rival_prediction: Mahalanobis distance from population centroid predicts undercoverage; bin_calibration_count does not.
cards.distinguishing_test: Partial correlation: coverage ~ bin_calibration_count controlling for Mahalanobis distance; H9 predicts bin_count significant (p<0.01), distance not.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Conformal theory: quantile estimation error ~ 1/sqrt(n); n<15 gives >25% relative error in 90% quantile.
minimum_data_needed: Mondrian bin assignments and calibration counts per subject
Subject feature vectors for rarity index
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in bins with calibration count <15 will have coverage ≤75% at 90% nominal; bins with count >50 will achieve ≥88%.
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between bin_calibration_count and coverage rate (Spearman ρ> -0.1, p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Weighted linear regression: coverage_rate ~ log(bin_calibration_count); weights = bin_size; test slope <0.
cards.falsification_test: Merge sparse bins (n<15) with nearest neighbor bin; if coverage for previously-sparse-bin subjects reaches nominal, sparsity mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Circadian phase at testing modulates stress reactivity such that afternoon-tested subjects show undercoverage because Mondrian calibration pools across circadian phases.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Afternoon testing (post-14:00) coincides with circadian cortisol dip → blunted HPA-axis stress response → different EDA/HRV pattern vs morning → Mondrian taxonomy ignores time-of-day → calibration intervals from mixed circadian phases don't match afternoon test distribution → undercoverage.
cards.causal_path: Afternoon test time (post-14:00) → circadian cortisol dip → blunted physiological stress response → Mondrian bin ignores time-of-day → calibration distribution ≠ afternoon test distribution → undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Time-of-day effects are mediated by alertness/fatigue, not circadian cortisol.
cards.rival_prediction: Subjective sleepiness (KSS) predicts undercoverage; test_time_of_day does not when KSS included.
cards.distinguishing_test: Mediation analysis: test_time_of_day → KSS → coverage; H10 predicts direct effect of time_of_day remains significant (p<0.05) after controlling for KSS.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Circadian cortisol amplitude ~50% peak-to-trough; stress reactivity modulation ~15-20%; Mondrian pooling dilutes but doesn't eliminate signal.
cards.testable_prediction: Afternoon-tested subjects (post-14:00) show coverage ≤80% at 90% nominal; morning subjects (pre-11:00) achieve ≥88%.
cards.failure_condition: No coverage difference between morning and afternoon groups after controlling for KSS (ANCOVA p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: ANCOVA: coverage_rate ~ time_of_day_group + KSS_score; test group effect.
cards.falsification_test: Stratify Mondrian calibration by time-of-day (morning/afternoon); if afternoon coverage reaches nominal, circadian mechanism confirmed; if not, falsified.
